rationale: This political science/public administration study evaluates general municipal governance styles, mayor-centric decision-making, aggregate fulfillment of basic governmental processes, and citizen-formed alternative/parallel governments across semi-urban municipalities in Michoacán, Mexico. Neither the title nor the abstract addresses household or community water or sanitation services, water/sanitation access outcomes, or legal/regulatory mechanisms governing water or sanitation access (failing C1, C2 narrow, and C4; E01 wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the study examines broad municipal governance and institutional governing styles (satisfying a literal governance factor reading of Criterion 2 in the abstract), it fails Criteria 1 and 4 completely because it concerns general municipal government processes and citizen parallel governments rather than household or community water or sanitation service access; therefore, the decision is exclude under both narrow and plain readings.
